direction: Evolve the single hook `score_ruin_nodes` as a multiplicative gated rank-power destroy-selection rule, with the rank exponent p made state-adaptive: p small (≈0.5–0.8, near-uniform randomized-agnostic spread) during early low-`iter_frac` exploration and p ramping up (≈1.5–2.0, sharp worst-removal focus) as `stagnation_ratio` grows. Gate by load utilization, depot proximity of the customer nearest in route, demand magnitude and route-length share, so that the ruin set prefers customers whose removal unlocks load re-balancing across routes. Keep the repair side fixed (deterministic Regret-2 + local intra_2opt + R2R acceptance) and keep the hook fully deterministic and state-only, so the gain is attributable to destroy prioritization alone under the 2000 ms budget where many more LNS iterations fit than the 500 ms reference.

operations.mechanism: Archive is empty (solver_count=0, no known signatures), so this round should establish the round-1 baseline on the mandated interface. The KB method entry (method-cvrp-m3-ruin-recreate-l3, content_sha256 94f7d539…) fixes the skeleton — CW + initial intra_2opt, Ruin(top-q) -> deterministic Regret-2 -> local intra_2opt -> R2R acceptance — and confirms `score_ruin_nodes` is the only evolvable hook with a multiplicative gate × rank-power form: score_i = rank_power(|removal_savings_i|/scale * gate_load * gate_depot * gate_demand * gate_rdist, p(iter_frac, stagnation_ratio)). Its blameworthy regime is the tight 25 ms budget (120/120 early-stop), and our target budget is 2000 ms — the mirror-image regime where first_feasible_ms ≈ 2–3 ms leaves nearly the whole budget for LNS iterations, so the anytime-curve payoff of a better destroy policy is maximal. Postprocess is fixed to `none` per the allowed set, and the repair layer stays untouched so any delta vs L3-ctrl is cleanly attributable to the evolved destroy score. Regret-2 feasibility handling follows method-cvrp-cheapest-regret-insertion, ensuring the 5-gate validator's dual-action probe (first_ruin_set A={1,2,3,4} vs B={3,4,5,6} on n=6, q=4) is satisfied by strict determinism and no global RNG.
